coupling: The overflow is a heap store one past the scanline area buffer (width columns, allocated by hb_raster_draw_render). cell_add still rejects col >= width, so a column equal to width is stored only when some call site passes a limit of width+1 AND some other edit makes that call site reachable for an edge that ends on column width. Commit 3cf1c63 (A) only retargets the clipped walk: the LTR window becomes the half-open range ending at x_org+width, and the RTL early-out moves one column right. Both still call cell_add with limit width, so the extra column is dropped and output is unchanged. Commit 8d1d10b (B) passes width+1 only on the two LTR closing cells (fast path and clipped path). With the original exclusive window and the original fast-path test cx1-x_org < width, neither call is reached with col == width. Commit f638356 (C) admits an LTR edge whose end column is exactly width onto the fast path, and passes width+1 only on the RTL clipped closing cell. The fast-path closing cell still uses limit width, and the RTL width+1 call is still skipped by the original cx1 > col_max return. Any one edit therefore cannot store column width. A+B stores it from the clipped LTR closing cell (A makes cx1 <= col_max true for that column; B passes width+1). A+C stores it from the RTL closing cell (A no longer returns when the end column is width; C passes width+1). B+C stores it from the fast-path LTR closing cell (C takes the fast path for end column width; B passes width+1). The same public draw (one LTR edge and one RTL edge, both ending on column width) hits all three paths, so reverting any single edited diff leaves a live overflow and reverting any two makes the input clean.
